items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Also I’ve been, besides Brookmeyer, very influenced, and I mean Gil Evans is just a master at everything. So I kind of looked at Gil Evans’ bands... And then, because of Gil Evans’ influence probably, I wanted to have a tuba.

ctx.x: Okay. Well thanks for taking some time today. And as the camera is kind of catching, you can see sketches all over the room. And I’m really glad to see real paper, to be honest with you, in this day and age.

Yeah, it’s part of the process for me and so the computer has its things and in many ways it’s made life easier as a composer and arranger, but for me, I still am — I have to work on paper. And so I write all my scores longhand, I do all my sketching and my full scores longhand, and then put it into the computer to make parts for the musicians. And I’m still in the quest of the best pencils that I can find and the paper you see, the King brand, this is all King brand manuscript paper. And it was used by Bob…
